title: anywaye fleet declaration
description: Schema for fleet.yml, core's machine-readable record of what the anywaye services actually publish. Where anywaye.manifest.schema.json describes one service's own anywaye.yml, this describes the fleet's: for each service repository, the event types its anywaye.yml declares, the commit that file was read at, and the catalog rows that exist as promises rather than as facts. It exists because the catalog was otherwise only ever compared against core's own example manifests, so a service could advertise any event type at all. `caf contract lint` reads this file rather than re-deriving the catalog; see docs/event-naming.md.

spec.description: The core spec this declaration was transcribed against. A reader who wants to know how stale it is compares this with the release it is on.

readOn.description: The day the manifests were read. Provenance is the whole value of the file: a claim about another repository is only good if you can say when it was true.

services.description: One entry per service repository, including a service that publishes nothing.

name.description: anywaye namespace name, equal to `name` in that service's own manifest and to the first segment of every event type it publishes.

repository.description: SSH remote of the service repository, as PLAN.md §1 requires of anything anywaye owns.

manifest.description: The file read. Every anywaye service names its manifest the same thing, and a linter resolving a service's declaration needs one path rather than a convention.

branch.description: The branch read. anywaye's primary branch is master everywhere (PLAN.md §1); a declaration taken from any other branch is not a declaration about the fleet.

sourceCommit.description: The full 40-character commit the manifest was read at. A short sha is not enough: the next reader needs to be able to re-read the exact bytes this claim was made from.

api.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document this service's manifest declares in `exposes.api`, transcribed. Same $defs as the manifest schema's, byte for byte, so a reader holding either file resolves the path the same way and a linter can compare the two without a translation table. OMITTED for a service whose manifest declares no `exposes` — and that is a claim about the manifest rather than about the disk, so a service that SHIPS a document without declaring it is recorded in its `notes` instead. Recording the path here for such a service would make core assert a field the manifest does not have, which is the defect this file exists to end.

events.description: Event types this service's manifest declares in exposes.events, in the grammar's three-segment form, for which core has shipped BOTH a catalog row and a payload schema. Conforming by construction: a manifest that declares a non-conforming type is recorded in manifestViolations instead, because the fix is the service's and core only owns the spec. A conforming type core has not finished is recorded in pendingCoreContract rather than here, because tests/test_specs.py asserts the catalog row and the payload schema and a type without them fails it.

cataloguedOnly.description: Event types core's catalog has a row for, that no service publishes yet. A catalog entry is a promise; this list is what keeps a promise from masquerading as a fact.

pendingCoreContract.description: The mirror image of `cataloguedOnly`, and the reason the word is the right one: a conforming event type this service's manifest DOES declare and the service DOES publish, for which core has not yet shipped the catalog row and the payload schema that make it usable. The debt is core's, and this list is what keeps it named rather than discovered. `tests/test_specs.py` asserts an entry here is a debt core really owes — a type with both a row and a schema does not belong, because that is an excuse for work already done. Whether the service really emits it is `sourceCommit`'s job and is not checkable from inside core; see D34 in DECISIONS.md. NO SERVICE IS IN THIS LIST as of core-23, which emptied it, and the property STAYS rather than being deleted with its entries: a list that appears when it is owed is worth more than one removed when it is not, and the next type a service declares and core has not answered needs somewhere checkable in both directions to go. The rule above is kept alive on data rather than on the entries, so an empty list does not quietly become a list that accepts anything.

manifestViolations.description: Types a service's manifest declares that violate the frozen grammar, recorded verbatim as the manifest spells them. They are never catalogued — a non-conforming type has no catalog row and no payload schema, because naming one here is not how you fix a publisher. The entry is deleted when the service's manifest is corrected, which is the acknowledgement.

telemetry.description: What this service exports and how it is pointed at a backend. Required, so "what is instrumented across the fleet" has one answer rather than six — the same reason the event list is required: a declaration that omits a service silences every check on it instead of failing one.

notes.description: One line on anything a reader of the numbers would otherwise have to go and find out — an absent `exposes`, a recorded open decision, a known debt.

serviceName.description: anywaye namespace rule: lowercase kebab-case, starting with a letter, no trailing separator.

eventType.description: <service>.<entity>.<action>, exactly three segments. Byte-identical to the same pattern in event-envelope.schema.json and anywaye.manifest.schema.json, which tests/test_specs.py asserts; see docs/event-naming.md.

openapiRef.description: Repository-relative path to an OpenAPI 3.1 document (.yaml, .yml or .json). No leading ./, no absolute paths, no URLs. Byte-identical to the same $defs in anywaye.manifest.schema.json, because this file transcribes `exposes.api` and two definitions of one path shape are two answers to the question a linter asks.

telemetryDeclaration.description: A service's observability declaration. `signals` is what the service exports TODAY, not what it could — the same honesty as `events` versus `cataloguedOnly`, because a fleet declaration that claims instrumentation a service does not have is worse than one that admits the gap. See docs/observability.md and schemas/telemetry/otel-endpoint.schema.json, which is the contract this points at.

endpointVariable.description: The one contract a self-hoster has to know: `<SERVICE>_OTEL_ENDPOINT`, uppercase, derived from the service name. The shipped collector is only this variable's default value, and unsetting it is a tested no-op rather than a code change (PLAN.md §7b). tests/test_specs.py asserts the name matches the service it sits beside.

signals.description: The OTel signals this service exports from its own code, to the endpoint named by endpointVariable. Empty is a legitimate and common answer, and it means exactly one thing: this service emits no signal of its own. The list describes the service's code; it is not a statement about what has been set up to receive those signals, and the two questions are answered independently.

probes.description: Whether the service serves HTTP and therefore owes the healthz/readyz split. A service that serves traffic and declares false is a service whose liveness is unstated, which is the gap darkroom does not have.

notes.description: One line on anything a reader would otherwise have to go and find out — which variable the service actually reads today, a recorded open decision, a known gap.
